subtopic: The 2008 Auction Rate Securities Market Collapse
source_evidence: The ARS market collapsed in February 2008 when lead underwriters chose not to step in to support the auctions.
answer: Auction rate securities (ARS) had interest rates reset through periodic auctions. After financial-market turmoil emerged in 2007, some auctions drew too few bidders to set a clearing rate. When lead underwriters stopped supporting the auctions, the ARS market collapsed in February 2008. Investors could be unable to sell their securities until an auction succeeded, leaving them with illiquid investments despite the securities’ long-term maturities.
